newsitem.title: USA: U.S. report to be released Wednesday - State Dept.
newsitem.headline: U.S. report to be released Wednesday - State Dept.

text.p: A long-awaited U.S. report on Nazi gold looted from victims of the Holocaust will be released on Wednesday, the State Department said on Tuesday.
The report will be made public by Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat and the State Department's chief historian, William Slaney, who compiled it.

The report involved the work of 11 government agencies and draws on more than 15 million documents, including thousands of documents that were declassified for the first time, John Dinger, a State Departemnt spokesman said.

He called it a "historical study looking at the facts -- our effort to try to determine, based on an enormous number of documents that we have in our files, in our archives, attempt to study and decide what happened."

On Sunday, Eizenstat told thousands of Holocaust survivors in New York that the report would pull no punches, saying: "This report will be objective. It will be fair and it will be tough in not only revealing the role of the neutrals but also shining the spotlight on the U.S. government. It will pull no punches."
Sources close to the State Department told Reuters last week the report would be very harsh on the Swiss role in the war as bankers and even money-launderers for the Third Reich.
Eizenstat has played a key role in negotiating the return of properties confiscated from Jewish victims of Nazi Germany to Holocaust survivors and their families.
